unit.title: Python: variables and types
unit.description: Giving a name to a value, changing it, naming rules, text and numbers, joining text

cards.definition: Stores the value on its right in the variable named on its left; it does not compare anything.
The usual way to name variables in Python: small letters, words joined by underscores.
Giving an existing variable a new value; the old value is replaced.
cards.example: score = 5 then score = 8: score now holds 8.

cards.definition: With two strings, the plus sign glues them end to end.
A string times a whole number repeats the text that many times.
Python refuses to add a string and a number with +: the number must be turned into text first.

exercises.explain: print(city) prints the value stored in the variable city, not the word city.
whyWrong: Without quotes, city is the name of the variable: its value is printed.
print shows the value, without quotes.
city received a value on the first line.

exercises.explain: score = 8 replaces the old value 5. The value stored last is the one printed.
whyWrong: The second line replaces 5 with 8.
= replaces a value; it does not add.
Numbers are not glued together like text.

exercises.prompt: Which name follows the usual Python style?
exercises.explain: Python names use small letters and underscores (snake_case). No spaces, no hyphens, and no digit at the start.
whyWrong: A name cannot contain a space.
A hyphen is read as a minus sign.
A name cannot start with a digit.

exercises.explain: With two strings, + joins them. The space inside "Hello " is kept.
whyWrong: The space is inside the first text, so it is kept.
The + is applied, it is not printed.
Joining two strings is allowed.

choices: An error: Python cannot add text and a number
It prints Age: 30 on one line
It prints nothing and moves on
exercises.explain: Python never mixes text and numbers with +. Turn the number into text first: "Age: " + str(30). The error is a TypeError.
whyWrong: Python refuses: it raises a TypeError.
Nothing is printed: the line fails before.
The line fails with an error message.

exercises.explain: A string times a whole number repeats the text: "ha" * 3 gives "hahaha", without spaces.
whyWrong: * repeats the text; it does not glue the number to it.
No space is added between the copies.
Multiplying a string by a whole number is allowed.

exercises.prompt: total = 0 creates a variable named total that holds the number 0.
exercises.explain: The name goes on the left, the value on the right, and = stores the value under that name.
A variable can be used in a calculation: price * 2 uses the value of price, 10.
whyWrong: Without quotes, the expression is computed.
price is 10, multiplied by 2.
price is a number, so * multiplies.

exercises.prompt: Build a line that stores the text "Lea" in a variable named first_name.
exercises.explain: first_name = "Lea": the name on the left, = then the value on the right.

exercises.prompt: This script stops with an error. Which line is wrong?
exercises.explain: age is a number and "Age: " is text: + cannot mix them. Write "Age: " + str(age).

exercises.prompt: Build a line that prints "Hi " joined with the variable name.
exercises.explain: print("Hi " + name) joins the text and the value of name.
